title: Quarterly business review - Wealth
transcript:
Michael Castillo: Morning everyone, let's get started. This is the Q2 wealth QBR, Wednesday July 15. Agenda is four things: flows and AUM, portfolio performance and rebalancing, client service and onboarding, and then action items. Grace is out today so I'm chairing. Linda, want to kick off with flows?
Linda Barnes: Sure. Net new assets for the quarter came in at about $41 million, which is ahead of the $35 million target. Most of that was from existing households consolidating outside accounts, only about $9 million was truly new relationships. Attrition was light, two households left for estate-driven reasons, nothing related to service.
David Montes: On the new relationship side, the pipeline is decent, about eleven prospects in late stage. I'd say we convert six or seven by end of Q3 if the referral flow from M&A holds up.
Michael Castillo: Good. Tricia, performance and rebalancing.
Tricia Kelly: Model portfolios outperformed their blended benchmarks by roughly 40 basis points net for the quarter on the balanced strategy. The conservative sleeve was flat to slightly behind, about 8 bps under, because we were short duration while the front end rallied in May. I'd flag that as a known positioning call, not a process issue.
Michael Castillo: Agreed. Did the June rebalance run clean in PortfolioMgr?
Tricia Kelly: Mostly. We had a delay on the June 30 run because PricingSvc was serving stale marks on a handful of municipal bonds, and since PortfolioMgr depends on it, the drift calculations were off for about 90 minutes. We reran after Technology cleared it. No trades went out on bad numbers, but I want a check that blocks the run if prices are older than a set threshold.
Jonathan Chandler: Can I add, that same morning my advisors saw drift flags that didn't make sense, and we had no idea whether to trust them. A banner in the tool would help.
Michael Castillo: Fair. Decision: we'll ask Technology for a stale-price guard on rebalance runs. Tricia, you own that request, and please file it with Sam Okafor's team with the June 30 timeline attached.
Tricia Kelly: Will do, I'll file it today.
Michael Castillo: Next, client service. James, you had a couple of items on the low-risk households.
James Anderson: Yes. First, {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0234}} is one of mine, long-standing low-risk brokerage client, been with us since 2017. They asked to move to quarterly statements delivered electronically and to update their contact preferences. I've confirmed the request, but I want to re-verify identity before changing anything on {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00480}}. I'll call them on the number we have on file, which is {{CLIENT_PHONE:c_0234}}, rather than responding to the email that came in.
Linda Barnes: Good call. Use the callback, not the inbound message. And log the verification in ClientHub.
James Anderson: Yes, already planned. I'll have it done by Friday.
Michael Castillo: Second item?
James Anderson: The review cycle. I have three annual reviews overdue from Q2 and I'd like to clear them before the end of July.
David Montes: I can take one of those off your plate if the household is already in my book. Send me the list.
James Anderson: Will do after the meeting.
Linda Barnes: On my side, {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0023}} has both a brokerage account, {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00050}}, and a cash management account, {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00051}}. They want to sweep idle cash from cash management into a short-term Treasury ladder. Risk profile is low so it fits, but I need Tricia to confirm the ladder construction.
Tricia Kelly: Happy to. I'd suggest staggering maturities over six months, so they keep liquidity. I'll send a one-page proposal to you by Monday.
Linda Barnes: Perfect. I'll send the summary to them at {{CLIENT_EMAIL:c_0023}} once you've signed off, and I'll set up a call to review.
Michael Castillo: Make sure the proposal goes through the normal suitability review before it goes out.
Linda Barnes: Of course.
Jonathan Chandler: One more topic from me, onboarding turnaround. Our average time from signed paperwork to funded account was nine business days this quarter, up from seven. The main drag was KYC clearance, waiting on document follow-ups.
David Montes: Right, and that's partly us. We send incomplete packets. I'd propose a pre-submission checklist for advisors so documents are complete the first time.
Jonathan Chandler: I can draft the checklist. I'll talk to the KYC team about what they reject most often.
Michael Castillo: Great, Jonathan owns that, draft by July 29. Let's aim to get back to seven days by end of Q3.
David Montes: Also worth noting KYCPipeline moves to Compliance ownership in October, so we should align the checklist with their intake requirements early.
Jonathan Chandler: Good point, I'll loop them in.
Michael Castillo: Let me recap action items. Tricia: file the stale-price guard request with Technology today, and send the Treasury ladder proposal to Linda by Monday. James: complete identity re-verification and the preference update for the brokerage client by Friday, and send David the overdue review list. David: take one of James's reviews and keep the pipeline conversions on track. Jonathan: draft the onboarding checklist by July 29 and consult Compliance. Linda: run the suitability review and client call on the cash sweep. Anything else?
Linda Barnes: Nothing from me.
Tricia Kelly: Nothing.
Michael Castillo: Thanks all. We'll reconvene for the Q3 review in October.
